modules.comments:
Small, dependency-light calculators for train horn setups on trucks and
other vehicles: how loud a horn is at a distance, how long an air tank
lasts and refills, and which copper wire gauge keeps the voltage drop in
budget.

This module re-exports everything from:

* `TrainHorn.Calc.Acoustics`: SPL at a distance (inverse-square law with
  optional air absorption), its inverse, the per-doubling loss and the
  addition of incoherent levels;
* `TrainHorn.Calc.AirSystem`: free-air volume (Boyle's law), tank
  runtime, blast count and compressor recovery time;
* `TrainHorn.Calc.Electrical`: AWG diameter, area, resistance, voltage
  drop and the smallest gauge for a drop budget;
* `TrainHorn.Calc.Validate`: length units and input checks.

Every function that takes user input returns `Either String Number` (or
`Either String` of a record or `Int`): `Left` carries a readable message
for invalid input such as a zero distance, a non-finite number or a
start pressure below the cut-off.

It is a faithful port of the Python package `trainhorn-calc` and is
tested against the same reference values to within 1e-9. Browser
versions of these calculators: [interactive calculators](https://train-horn.com/tools/).

Results are physics-based estimates, not measurements, and not legal
advice on horn use.

```purescript
import TrainHorn.Calc

splAtDistance 150.0 100.0 10.0                 -- Right 130.0
tankRuntimeSeconds 5.0 150.0 110.0 10.0 atmosphericPsi  -- Right 10.91...
map _.awg (suggestAwg 30.0 10.0 12.0 3.0 Feet 20.0)    -- Right "6"
```
modules.name: TrainHorn.Calc

declarations.comments:
SPL at `distance` with optional air absorption in dB/km (`>= 0`, see
`airAbsorptionDbPerKm`). The unit applies to both distances and is used
to convert them to metres for the absorption term.
declarations.title: splAtDistanceWithAbsorption

declarations.comments:
Free-field SPL at `distance` from a level `sourceDb` known at
`refDistance` (same unit for both distances):
`sourceDb - 20 * log10(distance / refDistance)`.

```purescript
splAtDistance 150.0 100.0 10.0 == Right 130.0  -- 150 dB at 10 ft -> 130 dB at 100 ft
```
declarations.title: splAtDistance

declarations.comments:
Free-field loss for each doubling of distance: `20 * log10(2)`, about
6.02 dB.
declarations.title: doublingLoss

declarations.comments:
Free-field level change in dB when the distance is multiplied by
`ratio` (`> 0`): `20 * log10(ratio)`. A ratio of 10 gives 20 dB.
declarations.title: distanceRatioLoss

declarations.comments:
Distance at which the level falls to `targetDb` with air absorption.
With absorption there is no elementary closed form, so the root is found
by bisection between the free-field answer and `refDistance` (the level
is strictly decreasing with distance), to a relative width of 1e-12.
declarations.title: distanceForSplWithAbsorption

declarations.comments:
Free-field distance at which the level falls to `targetDb`; the inverse
of `splAtDistance`: `refDistance * 10 ^ ((sourceDb - targetDb) / 20)`.
The result is in the same unit as `refDistance`.
declarations.title: distanceForSpl

declarations.comments:
Combines incoherent sources (for example two horns) into one level:
`10 * log10(sum(10 ^ (L_i / 10)))`. Two equal sources add about 3.01 dB,
not double the decibels. An empty array is a `Left`.
declarations.title: combineLevels

declarations.comments:
Approximate atmospheric absorption in dB/km at 10 degC and 70 % relative
humidity (an ISO 9613-2 table condition, from the ISO 9613-1 equations),
keyed by octave-band centre frequency in Hz. Train horn chords sit mostly
between about 250 Hz and 600 Hz, where absorption is only 1-2 dB/km.
Rounded, typical values: use them as a rough guide only.
declarations.title: airAbsorptionDbPerKm

declarations.comments:
Seconds of continuous horn time from `startPsi` down to `cutoffPsi`
for a horn drawing `hornCfm` of free air: `freeAirVolumeCuFt / hornCfm * 60`.

```purescript
tankRuntimeSeconds 5.0 150.0 110.0 10.0 atmosphericPsi  -- Right 10.9156...
```
declarations.title: tankRuntimeSeconds

declarations.comments:
Free air in cubic feet (at atmospheric pressure) released while a tank
of `tankGallons` US gallons drops from `startPsi` to `endPsi` gauge:
`tankGallons * 0.13368 * (startPsi - endPsi) / atmPsi`.

Arguments: tank gallons (`> 0`), start psi, end psi (`>= 0`, below
start), atmospheric psi (`> 0`, usually `atmosphericPsi`).
declarations.title: freeAirVolumeCuFt

declarations.comments: Cubic feet in one US liquid gallon: 231 in^3 / 1728 in^3.
declarations.title: cubicFeetPerGallon

declarations.comments:
Seconds for a compressor delivering a constant `compressorCfm` of free
air to refill the tank from `cutInPsi` to `cutOutPsi`:
`V_free / compressorCfm * 60`. Use the CFM rated at (or near) your
cut-out pressure; a 0 psi rating gives an optimistic time.

Arguments: tank gallons, cut-in psi, cut-out psi (`>` cut-in),
compressor CFM, atmospheric psi.
declarations.title: compressorRecoverySeconds

declarations.comments:
Recovery time when compressor output falls linearly with pressure, from
`cfmAtZeroPsi` at 0 psi to `compressorCfm` at `ratedPsi`:
`q(p) = q0 + b * p`. Integrating `dt = (V_tank / P_atm) dp / q(p)` gives

```
t = V_tank / P_atm * ln(q(p_out) / q(p_in)) / b * 60     (b /= 0)
```

Arguments: tank gallons, cut-in psi, cut-out psi, compressor CFM at the
rated pressure, CFM at 0 psi (`>=` compressor CFM), rated psi (`> 0`),
atmospheric psi.
declarations.title: compressorRecoveryLinearSeconds

declarations.comments:
Whole blasts of `blastSeconds` that fit in `runtimeSeconds`. A 1e-9
epsilon keeps exact divisions such as `0.9 / 0.3` from rounding down.
declarations.title: blastCount

declarations.comments:
Standard atmosphere at sea level in psi (14.696). Pass a lower value for
altitude.
declarations.title: atmosphericPsi

declarations.comments:
Result of `suggestAwg`: the chosen gauge, its drop in volts and percent,
and the inputs it was computed for.
declarations.title: WireSuggestion

declarations.comments:
Volts lost in a two-conductor copper run:
`amps * R_per_ft * 2 * oneWayLength`.

Arguments: amps (`> 0`), one-way length (`> 0`), AWG label, length
unit, conductor temperature in degC.
declarations.title: voltageDrop

declarations.comments:
Smallest copper AWG from `awgSizes` whose round-trip voltage drop stays

Arguments: amps, one-way length, system volts (`> 0`, typically 12 or
24), allowed drop in percent (`0 < x <= 50`, 3 is common), length unit,


modules.comments:
Sound pressure level (SPL) versus distance for a horn in open air.

A horn is treated as a point source in a free field. The level falls by
`20 * log10(d2 / d1)` dB (inverse-square law), with an optional
atmospheric absorption term:

```
L(d) = L_ref - 20 * log10(d / d_ref) - alpha * (d - d_ref) / 1000
```

where `alpha` is in dB per kilometre and the distances in the absorption
term are in metres.

Limits: no ground reflection, walls, wind or barriers; not valid very
close to the horn. Results are estimates, not measurements, and are not a
legal noise assessment.

keyed by octave-band centre frequency in Hz. Train horn chords sit mostly

Rounded, typical values: use them as a rough guide only.

modules.name: TrainHorn.Calc.Acoustics

modules.comments:
Onboard air system: tank runtime and compressor recovery.

A tank of volume `V` at absolute pressure `P` holds the same air as
`V * P / P_atm` at atmospheric pressure ("free air", Boyle's law). Gauge
pressures (psig) are made absolute by adding `P_atm`, so the free air
released between two gauge pressures is

```
V_free = V_tank * (P_start - P_end) / P_atm
```

Horn consumption and compressor output are rated in CFM of free air, so
`seconds = V_free / cfm * 60`.

Assumptions: isothermal expansion (fast blasts cool the air and give a
little less, so treat results as an upper estimate); the horn draws its
rated CFM at every pressure above the cut-off; the compressor is off while
the horn sounds; line, valve and leak losses are ignored.

declarations.comments:
Standard atmosphere at sea level in psi (14.696). Pass a lower value for
altitude.
declarations.title: atmosphericPsi

declarations.comments: Cubic feet in one US liquid gallon: 231 in^3 / 1728 in^3.
declarations.title: cubicFeetPerGallon

declarations.comments:
Free air in cubic feet (at atmospheric pressure) released while a tank

Arguments: tank gallons (`> 0`), start psi, end psi (`>= 0`, below
start), atmospheric psi (`> 0`, usually `atmosphericPsi`).

modules.name: TrainHorn.Calc.AirSystem

modules.comments:
Copper wire gauge (AWG) selection for 12 V / 24 V horn and compressor
circuits.

Resistances are computed from the AWG definition, not typed in from a
table:

* diameter (ASTM B258): `d(n) = 0.005 in * 92 ^ ((36 - n) / 39)`, where
  1/0, 2/0, 3/0, 4/0 are n = 0, -1, -2, -3;
* annealed copper at 20 degC (100 % IACS): `rho = 1.7241e-8 ohm*m`;
* `R = rho * L / A`, with `R_T = R_20 * (1 + 0.00393 * (T - 20))`.

The results agree with published solid-copper tables to within about 1 %
(10 AWG is 0.999 ohm per 1000 ft). Current flows out and back, so
`V_drop = I * R_per_length * 2 * one_way_length`.

Scope: this suggests the smallest gauge that meets a voltage-drop budget.
It does not check ampacity or fuse sizing; always fuse to protect the
wire you choose.

declarations.comments:
Gauges considered by `suggestAwg`, thinnest to thickest: the sizes
commonly sold as automotive primary wire and battery cable. Odd sizes
still work in the other functions.

declarations.comments: Annealed copper resistivity, 100 % IACS, at 20 degC, in ohm*m.

so callers can show the message to a user or chain checks with `do`
notation in the `Either String` monad.
